summary.headline: Rajratan Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin dipped on a ~INR10,000/ton steel price spike it could not pass on; FY26 sales volume up 18% to over 133,000 tons.
summary.overview: Management reported record sales tonnage for FY26 of more than 133,000 tons, up 18% YoY, from three locations (India, Thailand, and the newly merged USA subsidiary). Q4 EBITDA margin fell because steel wire rod rose by almost INR10,000/ton from January to March, which could not be passed on, while energy availability and cost also weighed. Management said the price increases have been passed on from April and expects margins to recover to 13-13.5% in Q1 FY27, with a sustained consolidated band of 13.5-14%. FY27 volume growth target is 17-18%, with Chennai capacity doubling to 60,000 tons by Q2 and steel cord (conveyor belt) trials starting in Q2.

EBITDA margin impact from unpassed raw material cost

financial_highlights.change: vs ~11.4% in prior quarter and 13.5% in Q2 per analyst

Low; Thailand BOI effective rate about 13.9%

segments.name: India (Pithampur/Indore and Chennai)
segments.commentary: India exports were just over 9,000 tons in FY26 and are targeted at about 15,000 tons in FY27. Indore/Pithampur and Thailand are running at about 90% utilisation, with Chennai peaking at 85-90% in March.

segments.name: Thailand
segments.commentary: Volume about 51,000 tons, guided to grow to 55,000-56,000 tons (10-11%) on debottlenecking. Q4 EBITDA margin about 10%. Thai BOI tax exemption applies beyond 36,000 tons of sales.

segments.name: USA (Rajratan USA, merged)
segments.commentary: Now consolidated; USA revenue cited at INR118 crore. Plan to grow North America about 30% in FY27. Around INR30 crore of cost for the second half is booked in the USA entity on FOB supply.

segments.name: Europe and Southeast Asia
segments.commentary: Europe to grow about 50% from a low base; Southeast Asia to grow 10-15%. Japan is an early new opportunity.

segments.name: Steel cord / wire rope (conveyor belt)
segments.commentary: 10,000 ton/year plant at Indore, about INR70 crore capex (INR50 crore spent). Expected top line about INR150 crore at peak, reached in about 2 years (FY29). Current EBITDA margin about 20% per management.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated volume growth of 17-18%, implying about 155,000 tons of total sales if conditions remain normal; excludes steel cord volumes.
Thailand FY27 volume 55,000-56,000 tons (10-11% growth); the balance of growth to come from India, mainly Chennai.
Consolidated EBITDA margin: management says to assume 13.5-14% sustainable; Q1 FY27 margin expected to return to 13-13.5%.
Chennai capacity to double from 30,000 to 60,000 tons by Q2 FY27, but FY27 sales expected around 34,000-35,000 tons, with gradual ramp-up.
PLI incentive (8% of incremental sales) is not included in projections; approval uncertain pending change in the ladder requested to the ministries.
Working capital requirement expected to stay high or rise; term loan to fall by under INR50 crore in FY27.
capex_capacity: Chennai: capacity to double from 30,000 to 60,000 tons by Q2 FY27 via balancing equipment; about INR25 crore more to be spent this year, with some machines already installed.

Steel cord (conveyor belt) at Indore: new shed built after the old 1989 shed was demolished; machines being installed, trials from Q2 FY27, full capitalisation by Q3 FY27; about INR50 crore spent with about INR25 crore more needed.
Consolidated capital WIP of about INR88 crore (standalone INR69 crore), of which about INR50 crore is steel cord and about INR20-25 crore is Chennai.
No additional capex plans for FY27 beyond Chennai and steel cord, per management.
State capital subsidy from MP government (30% of 2020 investment) received over 7 years, about INR3.5-4 crore a year; similar subsidy expected for steel cord and reduces the investment cost.
demand_pricing: Management says demand is robust in India, Thailand and globally; no GCC customers remain (exports to GCC are zero), and shipping disruption and port congestion at Singapore and Colombo are the main impact.
Tyre-sector market share back to 42-43% in India, from 35-37%; historic peak 43-44%.
Price increases passed on from April; realisation has moved above INR90,000/ton per the analyst's question, which management confirmed. Export pricing is set on global wire rod prices.
Competition: capacity exceeds demand, some global players may not survive, and new entrants must price lower; management says Rajratan's realisation is at the higher end.
Management expects the auto slowdown has not yet hit but expects a possible slowdown in April-May; this is not confirmed in the call.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins return to 13-14% and can they be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Q4 dip was from the Jan-Mar steel spike, now passed on from April; margin expected to return to 13-13.5% in Q1 FY27, and 13.5-14% is the sustainable consolidated band.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: A new consolidated USA subsidiary (Rajratan USA) is now merged; about INR30 crore of FOB shipping and logistics cost for the second half is booked there, not in Thailand. This could rise with export volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the tax rate low in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Thailand BOI privilege: income tax is exempt beyond 36,000 tons of sales, giving an effective rate of about 13.9% on the privileged company.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PLI status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is seeking a change in the PLI ladder after missing the year 1 and year 2 production targets; without approval, no PLI is assumed. If approved, it is 8% of incremental sales, about INR40-50 crore over 5 years.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the steel cord/wire rope business and what is its economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Steel cord for conveyor belts; 10,000 tons/year capacity, about INR150 crore peak revenue at about INR150/kg, reached in about two years (FY29), current EBITDA margin about 20%. Management says it is a pilot and not a big investment.

qa_highlights.question: Why expand Chennai when margins and pricing are under pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all Chennai customers are profitable, that market share must be defended, and higher output lowers variable cost; it said 13-14% is a decent margin for investment.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the rise in other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Gains from FX: the USD appreciated against the rupee on larger exports, and the Thai Baht strengthened, reflected in the balance sheet.

qa_highlights.question: Thailand and USA combined EBITDA margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Thailand Q4 EBITDA margin was 10% (corrected from 7.5% on the call). Management said Thailand and USA business had no substantial change and said it would respond separately on the combined figure.

risks_watch: Raw material cost volatility: wire rod rose about INR10,000/ton in Jan-Mar, and the company could not pass on costs immediately; margin depends on price pass-through.
Working capital and debt: export credit cycles of 45-60 days plus US duty costs push up working capital; management expects borrowing to stay at about 7-7.5% and not reduce.
Chennai ramp-up risk: 60,000 ton capacity, but FY27 sales targeted at only 34,000-35,000 tons; PLI approval unresolved, with two missed production targets.
Competitive pricing: excess global capacity, possible price cuts by competitors, and risk of volume price trade-off.
Shipping and geopolitics: Middle East conflict, port congestion and shipping delays; management flagged that Q1 dispatch shortages were expected to ease by end of April.
Steel cord/wire rope commercialisation: trials from Q2 FY27 and approvals still needed; volumes not in FY27 base case; wire rope contribution of 2,000-3,000 tons expected at most in FY27.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume and demand and on the return of margins from Q1 FY27, but guarded on specifics: management declined region-wise EBITDA, competitive pricing details, and several analyst follow-ups, and repeatedly caveated guidance with 'unless something major happens'. The tone was defensive on the Q4 margin miss and on the PLI, which is still unresolved.
key_quotes: So from January till March, the prices went up by almost INR10,000 a ton, which we could not pass on to the customer.
So you will see the margin coming back to 13%, 13.5% in the current quarter itself if everything remains normal.
We are not too optimistic about 18% to 20%, but we are also not pessimistic about 11, 12%.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 volume growth of 17-18% to about 155,000 t, backed by Chennai capacity doubling to 60,000 t by Q2 FY27 (though FY27 Chennai sales only 34,000-35,000 t), Thailand growth to 55,000-56,000 t, and tyre market share recovering to 42-43%; Indian exports target about 15,000 t, but no firm order book is cited.
